p:cNvPr.descr: An illustration of conversions of one-carbon units on tetrahydrofolate. In the bottom purple box, in the top middle is N5, N10-methylene-tetrahydrofolate, which is a hexagon, with a half hexagon on the left. At the top point is H over N. At the top right point is CH2. The bottom right point bonds up and right to H and down and right to CH2, which bonds down to N (in blue) with a 10 at the top. N bonds left to HC (in pink), which bonds up to N (in blue) with a 5 above, as the bottom point of the hexagon. The top left and bottom left points have a hexagon side jetting out. The left side is double-bonded. Below this are reversible arrows that points down to N5-formyl-tetrahydrofolate. These are identified as cyclohydrolase (in blue) (minor); spontaneous. To the right of the arrows is a curved arrow from ATP in an orange oval) to ADP [plus] Pi. In the arc of the arrow is N5, N10-methenyl-tetrahydrofolate synthetase (in blue). N5-formyl-tetrahydrofolate begins with a hexagon, with a half hexagon on the left. The hexagon is the same as described above, except on the bottom right point, where CH2 bonds down to N (in blue) over H, which bonds right. There is a 10 over the N. The bottom point is N (in blue) with a 5 above, which bonds down to C, which double bonds down and left to O and bonds down and right to H. C, O and H are all in pink. To the right of N5, N10-methenyl-tetrahydrofolate are reversible arrows, identified as cyclodeaminase (in blue). The top arrow pointing right has NH4+ (in pink) joining it. These arrows point right to N5-formimino-tetrahydrofolate, which is a hexagon, with a half hexagon attached on the left. The top point is H over N. The top right point is CH2. The bottom right point bonds up and right to H and down and right to CH2, which bonds down to N (in blue) over H, which bonds right. A 10 is over the N. The bottom point is N (in blue), which bonds down to HC, which double bonds down to HN (HC and HN are in pink). There is a 5 above the N. To the left of N5, N10-methenyl-tetrahyrdrofolate are reversible arrows, identified as cyclohydrolase (in blue). The top arrow pointing right also has another arrow jetting out to H2O. To the left of the arrows is N10-formyl-tetrahydrofolate. It has the same hexagon as decribed above, but CH2 on the bottom right point bonds down to N (in blue), which bonds right to nothing, and bonds down to C, which double bonds down and left to O and down and right to H. C, O, and H are in pink. This also has a half hexagon attached on the left. In the very right of the box is C, which bonds right to H, double bonds up to O, and bonds to the left to nothing. Above this box are reversible arrows, identified as N5, N10-methylene-tetrahydrofolate dehydrogenase (in blue). To the right of the arrows is a curved arrow pointing from NADPH in an orange oval [plus] H+ to NADPH. Above these arrows is another purple box that has the same hexagon and a half as mentioned below, but the bottom right has the CH2 bonding down to N (in blue), which bonds right to nothing, and bonds left to H2C (in pink), which bonds up to N (in blue) with a 5 above as the bottom point of the hexagon. This is N5, N10-methylene-tetrahydrofolate. In the far right of the box is –CH2OH in pink. Above this box is an arrow pointing up, identified as N5, N10-methylene-tetrahydrofolate reductase. To the right of the arrow is NADPH in an orange oval [plus] H+ pointing to NADP+ with a curved arrow The top purple box is identified as –CH3 (most reduced) in pink. This box has the N5-methyl-tetrahydrofolate. This has a hexagon, with a half-hexagon on the left. The top point of the hexagon is H over N. The top right point is CH2. The bottom right point bonds up and right to H and down and right to CH2, which bonds down to N (in blue) over H, which bonds right to nothing. A 10 is to the left of this. The bottom point is N (in blue) with a 5 above, which bonds down to CH3 (in pink). The life side is double bonded, At the top left point a side is jetting up and left, and at the bottom point, a side jets down and left. Above this box, at the top right, group transferred (oxidation state) is illustrated. To the left of the middle purple box are reversible arrows, identified as serine hydroxymethyltransferase (in blue)On the top arrow pointing right, there is a curved arrow from serine to glycine. Serine begins with C, which bonds left to H3N (plus sign on top of N), up to COO-, right to H, and down to CH2OH (in pink). Glycine begins with C, which bonds left to H3N (plus sign over N), up to COO-, right to H and down to H. There is another arrow jetting off from this arrow to HOH (OH in pink). The reversible arrows point left to tetrahydrofolate, which is the same hexagon and a half as mentioned in the first hexagon, only the bottom point of the hexagon has N over H, rather than N binding down to a pink CH3. Below this is a curved arrow, identified as N10-formyl-tetrahydrofolate synthetase (in blue), pointing to the bottom purple box. Formate (in pink) joins this arrow. Also, ATP in an orange oval points to ADP [plus] Pi with a curved arrow.
